ind.n: Large single premium paid then early surrender
ind.cx: Policy funded with lump sum and cancelled soon after, with refund to third party.
ind.ds: Policy funded with lump sum and cancelled soon after, with refund to third party.

ind.n: Premiums paid by unrelated third parties
ind.cx: Payers have no insurable interest or link.
ind.ds: Funds are paid or received, or instructions are given to pay, through parties with no evident link to the customer, contract, debt or insured interest. Includes third-party cheques, loan repayments, premiums, gaming funds and goods payments not matching the documentation.
ind.cn: Payments from or to unrelated third parties

ind.n: Policy loans or assignments to third parties
ind.cx: Rapid loans, assignments or beneficiary changes.
ind.ds: Rapid loans, assignments or beneficiary changes.

ind.cx: Paid in excess of required premium then withdrawn.
ind.ds: Paid in excess of required premium then withdrawn.

ind.n: Wash or matched trades between connected accounts
ind.cx: Same securities traded between related accounts at unrealistic prices.
ind.ds: Assets or securities are traded repeatedly between linked accounts or wallets at unrealistic prices.
ind.cn: Wash or matched trades between connected parties

ind.n: Securities deposited then transferred out without trading
ind.cx: Shares deposited and moved with no market activity.
ind.ds: Shares deposited and moved with no market activity.

ind.n: Trading in low-liquidity securities with unrelated parties
ind.cx: Illiquid instruments used to move value.
ind.ds: Illiquid instruments used to move value.

ind.n: Use of omnibus or nominee accounts
ind.cx: Positions hidden via omnibus or nominee structure.
ind.ds: Positions hidden via omnibus or nominee structure.

ind.n: Customer indifferent to investment performance or fees
ind.ds: Customer readily accepts poor terms, fees, losses, penalties or prices, showing little interest in performance, provenance or negotiation.
ind.cn: Customer indifferent to cost, return or value

ctl.ds: Monitors specialised products such as insurance, securities, safe deposit and prepaid instruments for surrender, free delivery, overpayment, assignment, matched trades and unusual access. It catches product-specific abuse.

Requires refunds, cancellations and aborted-deal repayments to go back only to the original payer and method after validation of the request. It blocks the use of refunds to convert illicit funds into clean payments.

Detects, restricts and challenges payments or deposits made by or to parties not named in the contract, account or invoice, and requires evidence of the relationship. It stops accounts and trades being funded by unexplained third parties.
Clusters customers, vendors and entities that share addresses, phones, devices, officers or bank details, including against staff records. It reveals common control and hidden relationships.

Requires documentary evidence of origin, legal sourcing, custody and conformity with responsible-sourcing standards, including for informal or recycled supply. It keeps illicitly sourced goods from entering the financed or traded chain.

Obtains independent valuations, appraisals or comparable-sale evidence for high-value assets, collateral and traded goods, and escalates large variances. It reveals deliberately mispriced assets used to move or conceal value.

Identifies the natural persons who ultimately own or control a legal entity or arrangement and verifies them using independent registers and documents, looking through intermediate layers. It is the core defence against anonymity achieved through layered or opaque structures.

Secures contractual rights to underlying client information for intermediated or pooled accounts, requires look-through on request and monitors pooled flows against expected activity. It gives visibility of who is really transacting behind an aggregate account.
Alerts when inflows are quickly moved out with little retained balance, including cash-in fast-out and rapid conversion or cash-out. It reveals accounts used as conduits for layering.

ctl.n: Purpose and intended nature of relationship
ctl.ds: Captures and challenges the stated purpose of the account, expected activity, volumes and geographies at onboarding, creating a baseline against which later behaviour is judged. Vague or implausible answers prompt further enquiry or decline.
Tailors training content and frequency to role and risk for finance, relationship, underwriting and compliance staff, with feedback of quality assurance findings. It builds baseline competence.
